doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Born near Tippo: the island farm in Tallahatchie County
summary: Allison and Audre describe the farm on Tippo Creek, its size, its origins and who owned it.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You’re from Tallahatchie County, Mississippi, near Tippo.
Yes. It was just a crossroad. I was born on a farm three miles south of Tippo.
It was called the island. Tippo Creek.
We also have with us, for the record, Audre Allison. You’ve been married over 60
years.
Yes.
62, it will be. Or is it already 62?
So I guess you’re qualified to act as a proxy.
Ok.
Well, how much... When I just think that he leaves something out, I should fill in? I don’t want to take over the thing.
Why was it called “the island”?
It was a creek around the island. Tippo Creek was... It encircled the island.
So the farm was on the island.
Yes.
How long had your family had the farm? When did they settle...
I don’t know. It was...
I think it was in 18-something that they first came there. Right?
Well, I don’t know... They came from Cascilla, I think, originally...
Cascilla in what state?
Tallahatchie County.
I see, Cascilla is a town in Tallahatchie County. Got it.
But the farm was more than an island. The farm is what, 1400 acres?
I don’t know.
Yeah.
So a big farm.
No, it wasn’t big...
Well, it’s not considered big for Mississippi. It’s not one of the really big farms.
But 1400 acres on an island 3 miles south of Tippo, Mississippi.
No, it wasn’t all on the island. The island was part of the farm, and still. Still there.
What was grown on the farm?
Cotton. Well, they used to grow cotton. But now they grow soybeans. But at that time we’re talking about, it was cotton.
So when you were a kid, cotton was still the crop.
Yes.
And you think your grandfather was the one who established the farm and cleared the land and so forth?
I don’t know.
Yes, that’s what I’ve always heard, that it was... I mean, there may have been some part of it that was (?). But they kept clearing...
Well...I don’t know how much was cleared, and how much was there originally.
